brief: LexiRead is an offline-first Android e-book reader with language learning built in: it imports EPUB, PDF and FB2 from a dozen catalogues, paginates them itself, and lets you look up and save any word without leaving the page. The mark has to survive a 48 px launcher slot and still read as 'a book you keep your place in'.
criteria: Success: recognisable at 48 px, distinct from Openlib's mark without abandoning its book-and-bookmark reading, works in one colour, and does not depend on the wordmark to be understood.

concepts.name: Bookmark Right
concepts.idea: Openlib's book-and-bookmark reading, mirrored and recoloured: a navy slab with a gold ribbon on the right, on a warm cream ground.
rationale: One slab and one ribbon: legible at 48 px with no detail that disappears
The ribbon moves to the right and the palette becomes LexiRead's own, so it is a variation rather than a copy
Built from three primitives on a 256 grid, so every density renders crisply
A separate mono cut punches the ribbon out of the slab, so the mark survives one-colour and Android themed icons
The wordmark is gone from the icon: it was illegible at 48 px and a mark should not need one

recommendation: Bookmark Right, as approved. Shipped as an adaptive icon (cream background layer, mark foreground layer sized inside the 66 dp safe circle, plus a monochrome layer) and as legacy WebP rasters at all five densities.
next_steps: Launcher icon replaced in app/src/main/res — adaptive icon layers plus all five mipmap densities
Check the cream ground against the app's navy chrome on a real device
Run a trademark search before publishing; this is a variation on Openlib's mark
